layer.ip.nat.kid: Your router swaps the sender address for your home’s address, and remembers who asked.
layer.ip.nat.nerd: NAT: source 192.168.1.23:51034 is rewritten to 203.0.113.7:51034 and stored in the connection table.
layer.ip.unnat.kid: Your router looks up who asked for this and changes the address back to your phone.
layer.ip.unnat.nerd: NAT reverse: destination 203.0.113.7 is rewritten back to 192.168.1.23 from the connection table.
layer.ip.bridge.kid: The access point doesn’t read the address. It just passes the parcel on to the router.
layer.ip.bridge.nerd: The AP is a layer-2 bridge: it swaps the Wi-Fi frame for an Ethernet frame and leaves IP untouched.
layer.ip.read.kid: This box reads the address and picks the best way onwards.
layer.ip.read.nerd: Routed: longest-prefix match in the FIB, TTL − 1, a new link frame for the next hop.
layer.ip.arrived.kid: Arrived! This is the right address.
layer.ip.arrived.nerd: Destination reached: hand the payload up to TCP.
